input: Source an illustrator for my children's book

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The number of illustrations and whether cover art, spot illustrations, or full-page spreads are needed dramatically changes the workload and shapes what kind of illustrator to look for.
Knowing the target age group of the book's readers determines the visual complexity, character style, and tone the illustrator must be able to deliver.
Art style (e.g. whimsical, realistic, flat/graphic, watercolour) is the single biggest filter when evaluating illustrator portfolios — without this, any shortlist is meaningless.
Budget sets which tier of illustrators is realistic and whether the user should look at agencies, freelance platforms, or emerging artists.
Whether this is self-publishing, a traditional publisher deal, or a submission package changes rights requirements, contract norms, and urgency.
Knowing where the user wants to search (e.g. Reedsy, Upwork, Instagram, local networks) determines the immediate next action and the sourcing strategy.
Understanding what a successful hire looks like — speed of delivery, style match, communication, experience level — sets the criteria for evaluating and choosing between candidates.

gold.taskTitle: Source an illustrator for my children's book
gold.taskDescription: Find and hire a suitable illustrator to create artwork for the user's children's book project.

questions.title: How many illustrations does the book need?
questions.description: Establish the total illustration count and types (e.g. full-page spreads, spot art, cover) to define the scope of work for a prospective illustrator.

questions.title: What age group is the book written for?
questions.description: Identify the target reader age (e.g. 0-3 board book, 4-8 picture book, 8-12 middle grade) as this determines the visual style and complexity required.

questions.title: What art style are you envisioning for the book?
questions.description: Pin down the preferred visual style (e.g. whimsical watercolour, bold flat graphics, detailed realism) to use as the primary filter when reviewing portfolios.

questions.title: What is your budget for the illustration work?
questions.description: Clarify the total budget or per-illustration rate the user can offer, which determines which platforms and experience tiers are realistic to target.

questions.title: Is this for self-publishing or a traditional publisher?
questions.description: Determine the publishing route, as this affects rights ownership, contract structure, and how urgently an illustrator needs to be secured.

questions.title: Where do you want to search for illustrators?
questions.description: Identify preferred sourcing channels (e.g. Reedsy, Upwork, Instagram, illustration agencies, referrals) to focus the sourcing strategy on the right platforms.

questions.title: What matters most when choosing the final candidate?
questions.description: Establish the user's top hiring criteria — such as portfolio strength, turnaround time, communication style, or prior children's book experience — to guide the final decision.
